lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The summer noise is thin, but the Leafs have at least one live wire: Patrik Laine remains a gamble worth taking, a reminder that this roster is still being shaped in real time rather than merely discussed in theory. Toronto's 32-36-14 finish in 2025-26 left no room for nostalgia, and the front office has spent the deep offseason probing for bite up front and more certainty behind the stars. Laine is the kind of name that can tilt a lineup - if the fit is right and the body holds up. That is the whole trick now. Auston Matthews, William Nylander and John Tavares remain the gravitational pull, but the intrigue is in the supporting cast and the prospect pool, where Victor Johansson and the rest of the top 10 are being judged on upside, not applause. By camp, the only thing that will matter is whether this new mix looks harder to play against.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' winter has a pulse, and it's coming from the bullpen door swinging open - Toronto has leaned hard on roster churn, then turned a sharper edge by claiming Paul Sewald and recalling Chase Lee as it tries to patch late-inning leaks. That's the most important move in the last 48 hours - a sign the club is still hunting for certainty, not comfort. This is a team that finished 2026 at 63-99, and the record explains the urgency: the front office has to rebuild depth without wasting another summer. José Soriano gives the rotation a live arm and, with team control through 2028, a reason to believe the next core can take shape fast. The real question now is whether Toronto can pair that arm with a steadier bullpen and a healthier lineup. Watch the Sewald-Soriano ripple effect - and whether more relief help follows.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet is the right word for August, but Toronto's offseason at least has a pulse. The NBA Cup draw dropped with the Raptors grouped against Orlando, Detroit and Milwaukee - a tidy little measuring stick before the real work begins. For a club sitting at 46-36 and 5th in the East, the next step is less about fireworks than fit, and the new calendar underscores that. The chatter now turns to the guards: who can screen, who can bend a defense, who can keep the offense from flatlining when the starters rest. Add in the recent two-way move for Trey Jemison III and the roster picture feels sturdier, if still unfinished. Training camp opens in Quebec City on September 28, and that's when the sorting starts for real.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Camp has found its bite, and Washington's latest joint work with Miami sharpened the picture in a hurry - Jayden Daniels looked poised and the Commanders' defense, by every account, won the day. That matters because this is a team still sorting its lines in the mud: Laremy Tunsil is sidelined with a triceps issue, Nick Allegretti has been nursing a calf strain, and the center spot has become the loudest worry in Ashburn. Daniels' comfort in the offense is the headline, though, and it is no accident that Dan Quinn has been measured afterward. The Commanders are in training camp, not yet in the standings, but the hierarchy is being written now. Watch the offensive line shuffle and the preseason debut Friday against Detroit - that is where the first real answers should start to show.

article.title: Thursday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are still sifting through a busy offseason, and Patrik Laine remains the most eye-catching name in the unsigned forward market if Toronto wants another swing on skill up front. There is also a younger layer to watch, with prospect Victor Johansson showing up at No. 14 in one Leafs ranking as the club keeps reworking its depth chart.

The Blue Jays have a little momentum to carry into the morning after back-to-back coverage of a wild-card push and bullpen help, plus a third straight win over Boston in another report. The Raptors are in the deep offseason, with their NBA Cup group now set alongside the Pistons and Magic, while the Commanders are in camp and drawing attention after a dominant joint practice with Miami and a roundup of the main storylines from training camp.
